title: Reduce GPU memory and workspace via arena tuning, activation checkpointing, and scratch buffer reuse for continuous batching
author: Priya Natarajan
description: This PR reduces GPU memory and transient workspace usage for the inference runtime by tuning the arena allocator, enabling targeted activation checkpointing for decoder-heavy layers, and reusing scratch buffers across continuous batching windows. Motivation: large sequence and multi-request workloads were causing OOMs and excessive workspace fragmentation on dense GPU pool nodes, impacting latency SLOs and reducing packing efficiency. Changes include arena allocation threshold heuristics to keep hot pools compact, per-model configurable activation checkpointing with safe fallback for short sequences, a thread-safe scratch buffer pool that is reused across batch windows, and improved KV cache memory accounting to avoid double-counting transient workspace. The patch adds microbenchmarks and perf suites to validate memory reduction across our standard models (Llama variants and MPT) and includes a rollout plan and feature flags for canarying. Results: 18-35% GPU memory reduction on 8k token workloads, up to 25% fewer OOM retries during sustained continuous batching, end-to-end throughput unchanged or slightly improved (+3-7%) for large-batch scenarios, and latency P50/P95 within SLO after tuning. Checklist: [x] unit tests added, [x] perf benchmarks, [x] feature flags and config knobs, [x] documented arena tuning guidance, [x] rollout plan for Dedicated clusters. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserved for current customers, flags required to enable aggressive checkpointing. See related Linear items ENG-1423 and ENG-1498 and support ticket SUP-789.
commits_summary: tune arena allocation thresholds and bucket sizes
reuse scratch buffers across continuous batching windows
add per-model activation checkpointing toggle and safe fallback path
improve KV cache memory accounting and expose debug metrics
add GPU perf benchmarks and CI perf job
update docs/perf/arena_tuning.md and add rollout notes
review_conversation: Alex Gomez: Can you explain how the arena thresholds were chosen and whether they are sensitive to heavy multi-tenant nodes?

Priya Natarajan: Thresholds derived from production histograms (sequence length and allocation size). Added a knob to scale aggressiveness per-node and preserved a conservative default for multi-tenant Dedicated nodes.
Samir Patel: I saw a race on the scratch pool in the first run of unit tests, looks like double-free under stress. Please add a concurrent test.
Priya Natarajan: Good catch, added a thread-safety wrapper and concurrent stress test. Rerun CI shows green.
Lina Chen: Activation checkpointing can change memory/time tradeoffs; have you run the eval suite on small prompts to ensure latency regressions are within acceptable bounds?

Priya Natarajan: Yes, included eval runs for short and long sequences; short sequences fall back to non-checkpointed path and are unchanged. Added docs and a feature flag for canarying aggressive checkpointing.
merge_details: Merged by squash via web UI after approvals from Alex Gomez and Samir Patel. Merge method: squash. No follow-up changes required.
release_notes: Reduced GPU memory usage and workspace fragmentation by tuning arena allocator, enabling optional activation checkpointing, and reusing scratch buffers; add feature flags and rollout guidance. Improves memory headroom for large-sequence continuous batching workloads.
